 Canadian authorities are offering a reward of up to $250,000 for information leading to the arrest of Satinderjeet Singh, also known as Goldy Brar, a murder suspect who is on the FBI's Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list. The Bolo Program, a Canadian public safety initiative that works with law enforcement to locate wanted fugitives, ranked Singh at the top of its new list of Canada’s 25 most wanted and announced the reward in a press release on Thursday. Singh is wanted in connection with the 2023 killing of 39-year-old Sukhdool Singh Gill in Winnipeg, Manitoba, while U.S. authorities separately accuse him of helping lead the Lawrence Bishnoi Organized Crime Group and have offered up to $1 million for information leading to his arrest. The Canadian reward is available to anyone who provides information leading to Singh’s arrest in either Canada or the United States. “I believe I speak on behalf of Canadian Law Enforcement when I say that we will aggressively defend our cities, and our country, against this kind of violence. We don’t accept it, and we will be relentless when it comes to pursuing these types of investigations,” Winnipeg Police Service Deputy Chief Cam Mackid said in the press release. Singh was added to the FBI list on September 28 over his alleged role in the Lawrence Bishnoi Organized Crime Group, which U.S. authorities have linked to targeted assassinations, extortion and drug trafficking across the U.S. and Canada. His case has involved extensive cross-border cooperation, with the FBI, Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) and other U.S. and Canadian law enforcement agencies working together to investigate the group and locate fugitives. When Singh was added to the list, the agency also announced a reward of up to $1 million for information leading to his arrest. “Satinderjeep Singh, also known as Goldy Brar, is a dangerous individual, and the FBI and our partners have made it our priority to apprehend him, which is why we’re adding him to the FBI’s list of Top Ten fugitives and offering a reward of up to $1 million dollars for his capture,” FBI Los Angeles Field Office Assistant Director in Charge Patrick Grandy said in September. “The amount of attention this list will bring to his face and description cannot be overstated; his photo will be found on every FBI-affiliated website and social media platform, and will be publicized on every phone around the world until he’s caught.” Operation Hard Ball: What to Know Before Singh was added to the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list, U.S. federal authorities spent years investigating transnational organized-crime groups accused of killings, extortion, drug trafficking and other crimes across several countries in an effort dubbed Operation Hard Ball. The investigation culminated in July with three indictments charging 37 people and a coordinated law enforcement operation that resulted in 24 arrests in the U.S., Canada and Europe. Prosecutors allege that Singh and Lawrence Bishnoi ordered the June 2023 killing of a prominent political and religious figure outside a Sikh temple in Surrey, British Columbia. The operation also highlights the cross-border cooperation involved in pursuing Singh. The FBI and RCMP investigated the cases alongside multiple U.S. and international agencies, while the RCMP conducted a parallel investigation into South Asian organized crime.  Before Singh was added to the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list, U.S. federal authorities spent years investigating transnational organized-crime groups accused of killings, extortion, drug trafficking and other crimes across several countries in an effort dubbed Operation Hard Ball. 
 The investigation culminated in July with three indictments charging 37 people and a coordinated law enforcement operation that resulted in 24 arrests in the U.S., Canada and Europe. Prosecutors allege that Singh and Lawrence Bishnoi ordered the June 2023 killing of a prominent political and religious figure outside a Sikh temple in Surrey, British Columbia.
 The operation also highlights the cross-border cooperation involved in pursuing Singh. The FBI and RCMP investigated the cases alongside multiple U.S. and international agencies, while the RCMP conducted a parallel investigation into South Asian organized crime.
 Who Else Is on FBI’s Ten Most Wanted Fugitives List?
 In addition to Singh, the nine other people on the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list are:
 Trung Duc Lu: Wanted on charges related to kidnapping, racketeering, extortion and marijuana distribution.
 Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores: Wanted for allegedly conspiring to traffic large quantities of methamphetamine, cocaine, heroin and marijuana into the U.S., as well as firearms offenses.
 Giovanni Vicente Mosquera Serrano: Wanted on federal international cocaine-trafficking and terrorism-support charges.
 Joseph Matos: Wanted on federal racketeering-related murder and firearms charges.
 Ruja Ignatova: Wanted on federal wire fraud, money laundering and securities fraud charges.
 Wilver Villegas-Palomino: Wanted on federal narco-terrorism and international cocaine-trafficking charges.
 Yulan Adonay Archaga Carias: Wanted on federal racketeering, cocaine-importation and machine-gun charges.
 Bhadreshkumar Chetanbhai Patel: Wanted on murder, assault and weapons charges, and unlawful flight to avoid prosecution.
 Omar Alexander Cardenas: Wanted for murder and unlawful flight to avoid prosecution.
 What Happens Next
 Anyone with information about Singh is urged to reach out to law enforcement officials in Canada or the U.S. In Canada, a tip line number has been created at (431) 334-9160. The FBI encourages anyone with information to contact the FBI's toll-free tip line at 1-800-225-5324.
